verdict.label: concordant
verdict.rationale: Both sources address myocardial infarction risk with sulfonylurea treatment in type 2 diabetes and each explicitly reports no increased risk. Source A (meta-analysis of RCTs) states sulfonylureas were 'not associated with increased risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0.92 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.12])' and concludes no increased risk for myocardial infarction. Source B (propensity-matched cohort, sulfonylurea vs metformin monotherapy) states sulfonylurea monotherapy 'was not associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.04, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.85-1.25)'. Both assertions are explicit no-difference conclusions; the slightly different point estimates (0.92 vs 1.04) and different designs/comparators do not create an opposition, since both authors explicitly conclude no increased MI risk. Extraction fields on both sides match their sources (no material errors).

source_evidence.quote: Sulfonylureas were also not associated with increased risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0.92 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.12])

After matching, sulfonylurea monotherapy, compared with metformin monotherapy, was not associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.04, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.85-1.25)

diagnostics.notes: Both claims verified against their abstracts: A's Peto OR 0.92 (0.76-1.12) with explicit no-increased-risk wording, and B's HR 1.04 (0.85-1.25) with explicit no-increased-risk wording, are correctly extracted. Comparability holds: same drug class (sulfonylureas), same outcome (myocardial infarction), both between-group contrasts. Design and comparator differences (RCT meta-analysis with unnamed comparator vs observational cohort vs metformin) are contextual but do not affect the concordant explicit no-difference conclusions.
